prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Green Party Manifesto 2005 — Summary (ideological framing preserved)

Vision
Build a sustainable society grounded in social, economic and environmental justice. Reverse privatisation and marketisation of public services; defend civil liberties; put peace, equity and climate action at the heart of government.

Economy
- Tackle inequality via steeply progressive income tax (e.g., 50% over £50k; 60% over £100k) and more Corporation Tax bands (up to 40% for largest firms). Tax unearned wealth: progressive, recipient-based Inheritance Tax; abolish National Insurance and tax all income fairly.
- Democratise land and local revenue: pilot Land Value Tax to replace Council Tax/Uniform Business Rates.
- Replace VAT with revenue-neutral eco-taxes tied to resource use, pollution and waste (including aviation fuel), aligning prices with environmental costs.
- Localise economies: community banks, credit unions, local currencies; support SMEs and co‑ops; oppose euro entry; reform WTO.
- Create green jobs through renewable energy, zero-waste and low‑carbon transport; defend workers’ rights and shorter hours.
- Measure real progress beyond GDP (e.g., ISEW/MDP).
- Introduce universal Citizen’s Income and Citizen’s Pension.

Energy and climate
- Adopt Contraction & Convergence: cut UK CO2 20% by 2010, 50% by 2020, 85% by 2030; move to full carbon trading within C&C.
- Carbon Tax based on fuel carbon content; protect low‑income users via tariff reform.
- 40% of energy from renewables by 2020; redirect nuclear subsidies to renewables; mass deployment of solar, wind and biogas.
- Cut demand: Warmer Homes Act (30% domestic demand reduction in 10 years); all councils as Smart Energy Councils; Cabinet post for climate policy.
- Close nuclear as stations reach end of life.

Welfare, work, housing
- Universal, non‑means‑tested Citizen’s Income; integrate benefits over time; retain/add disability support; move to include Housing Benefit.
- Citizen’s Pension, earnings‑linked and universal; abolish Pension Credit means‑testing.
- Support families: simplify child support; raise Child Benefit; end 48‑hour opt‑out; move toward 35‑hour week; expand Sure Start.
- Boost affordable housing: reinvest sale receipts; support self‑build co‑ops; LVT reform; upgrade efficiency/insulation.

Health and education
- Restore NHS to universal, comprehensive service; end PPPs, foundation hospitals, marketisation and GATS encroachment.
- Abolish prescription charges; restore free eye tests and NHS dentistry; expand holistic care; prioritise prevention and mental health.
- Fund to at least pre‑2004 EU average; hypothecated NHS Tax; long‑term savings from defence cuts.
- Education for life: increase funding, expand Children’s Centres; scrap tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; abolish SATs; adopt Individual Learning Plans.

Transport
- Plan for modal shift: walking/cycling → rail/trams/buses → freight → cars; cut road traffic 10% by 2010; redirect £30bn from roads to transit.
- Re‑regulate buses; integrate ticketing; redesign towns for proximity and active travel; end “school run” dependence.
- Bring rail and Tube back to public ownership; expand rail and light rail; grow rail freight.
- Price true costs of motoring: extend congestion/road pricing; raise fuel duty; retire tax disc; size/pollution‑based freight duty; fund clean R&D.
- Curb aviation growth: no new runways, ban night flights, EU‑wide fuel tax, UK emissions tax for domestic flights, higher APD.

Environment, food, farming
- Zero Waste Strategy: ban incineration; enforce recycled content; Zero Waste Agency; target 60% household recycling by 2010; eco‑taxes on toxics and fossil fuels; Environmental Protection Commission.
- Precautionary principle on GM, xenotransplantation, nanotech; end patents on life; strengthen chemicals rules.
- Animal welfare: end live exports; ban battery eggs and fur; tougher broiler rules; replace vivisection.
- Local, secure food: Organics Target Bill (30% by 2012); abolish/replace CAP and CFP with support for organic, local, biodiversity‑rich systems; ban GM food; curb supermarket abuses with a binding Code and stronger OFT action.

Crime and justice
- Prevent crime by tackling social/environmental causes: safer urban design, youth provision, rapid repair, staffed public spaces; treat drugs as a health issue; oppose ID cards.
- Community policing, local accountability, more stations and neighbourhood committees; restore “social agents” (e.g., park keepers).
- Strong gun control: clear lethality thresholds; prohibit handguns/automatic weapons; regulate deactivated arms; single, safety‑first licensing.
- Expand restorative justice; strengthen human rights; combat hate crime and violence against women; EU‑wide disability rights.

Democracy
- Devolve power: revitalise local councils with PR and LVT; citizen‑initiated referenda and recall.
- PR for Westminster; fully elected House of Lords.
- Written constitution; disestablish Church of England; remove monarchy’s formal powers.
- Oppose costly, illiberal national ID cards.

Peace, security, international policy
- Ethical foreign policy: diplomacy, UN peacekeeping, equity and sustainability; withdraw UK forces from Iraq and support UN‑led stabilisation.
- Cut defence to EU average; end arms export subsidies; negotiate an Arms Trade Treaty; scrap nuclear weapons and ban CBRN/environmental arms.
- Justice and stability: aid at 1% of GNI by 2010; cancel debts of 52 poorest nations; Tobin tax; equity via North‑South carbon trading.
- Reform UN: end permanent Security Council seats/vetoes; democratise IMF/World Bank for poverty prevention and sustainability.
- Transform trade: replace/overhaul WTO with a General Agreement on Sustainable Trade favouring localisation, fair labour and environmental protection.
- Humane asylum/migration: right to work and benefits, faster fair decisions, independent appeals; ratify UN Migrant Workers Convention; uphold Refugee Convention.
